//: Hand-written notes on openDAW's devices: what a producer weighs when choosing one, which openDAW's API and manual don't say (STRATEGY.md, 'What agents know': the catalog's hand-written lines).
Keyed by device type as the snapshot names it (the box name without 'DeviceBox' or 'Box'). openDAW's own names, descriptions and parameters come from openDAW, not from here.

Fields: sound (the timbre or what it does to a sound, typical rather than per preset), roles (what it's used for in a track), genres (where it's commonly heard), evokes (classic gear or sounds it recalls), words (how producers describe what they want when this is the answer), limits (what it can't do, or when to pick something else). opaque: its sound depends on content we can't read (a script, a plugin, a model file); name it, don't describe it.

Written 2026-11-06 from openDAW's manual pages and general production knowledge, not from listening. A synth's sound depends on its settings: these describe its character and range, not a given patch.

Vaporisateur.sound: Classic two-oscillator analog-style subtractive synth: saw, square, triangle and sine through a resonant low-pass filter, with unison detune for width. Warm and familiar rather than exotic; can be fat, soft or buzzy depending on waveform and cutoff.
evokes: Juno- and Minimoog-style analog polysynths and monosynths
Vaporisateur.limits: Not for metallic, bell-like or glassy tones (Tubular or Neon) or acoustic-sounding ones (Korpus). One low-pass filter, so no band-pass or formant colours.

Cubed.sound: Monophonic acid bass synth in the spirit of the Roland TB-303: one saw or square oscillator into a resonant ladder filter, with accent and slide. Rubbery, squelchy and resonant; screams as resonance and env mod go up.
Cubed.limits: One voice: no chords or pads. Its character comes from accents and slides: from timeline notes, velocity 100+ accents and overlapping notes slide, so flat, separated notes sound tame.

Neon.sound: Phase-distortion synth after the Casio CZ series: timbre sweeps from a pure cosine to saw, square and resonant shapes without a filter. Bright, glassy, slightly hard-edged digital character; ring mode gives bells and clangs.
Neon.limits: Brightness is shaped by envelopes, not a cutoff knob, so 'darker' means changing the DCW amount, not a filter. Less warm than Vaporisateur.

Tubular.sound: Six-operator FM synth compatible with the Yamaha DX7 (Dexed's engine). Clear, bright, often metallic or bell-like; the classic FM electric piano, tines, mallets, plucked basses and hard digital brass.
evokes: Yamaha DX7 (E.Piano 1, tubular bells, FM bass)
Tubular.limits: Hard to make warm and analog-fat; its sound lives in its operators and algorithm, so it's best changed by loading a patch rather than tweaked. Can sound thin or harsh in the highs.

Korpus.sound: Physical modelling, no samples: a mallet, pick, bow or breath excites bars, bells, membranes, plates or strings. Organic and acoustic-sounding: marimba, vibraphone, gamelan, glass, bowed and plucked strings, flutes.
evokes: marimba, vibraphone, kalimba, gamelan, shakuhachi, glass harmonica, nylon and steel-string guitar
Korpus.limits: Not a realistic sampled instrument; not for big synth bass or supersaw leads. Its sound changes a lot with the exciter and material, so name the model chosen when describing it.

Nano.sound: Plays one sample across the keyboard, with a loop and an envelope. Sounds like whatever sample is loaded, repitched: natural near its root key, chipmunk or slowed further away.
Nano.limits: One sample: no velocity layers or round robin, so realistic pianos or strings need Soundfont. Describe it by its sample, not by the device.

Playfield.sound: Drum machine and sampler: one sample per pad, each on its own MIDI note. Sounds like its kit; the pad names say which drum is which.
evokes: MPC- and 808/909-style drum machines, depending on the kit loaded
Playfield.limits: Its style comes from the kit and the pattern; read the pad names before describing it.

Soundfont.sound: Plays .sf2 multi-sample instruments: pianos, strings, brass, organs and General MIDI sets. Realistic within the quality of the soundfont; GM sets can sound dated.
Soundfont.limits: Needs a soundfont file and preset; describe it by the preset name. No soundfonts in the study's sample library yet.

Tape.sound: The audio track: plays recorded or imported audio regions as they are. No sound of its own.
Tape.limits: Describe it by its regions' samples. Not played by notes.

InstrumentComposite.sound: Layers several instruments on the same notes, each with its own effects and level. Sounds like the sum of its layers.

Apparat.sound: A user-written script instrument; its sound depends entirely on the script.
Apparat.limits: Name the script, never describe its sound.

MIDIOutput.sound: Sends notes to external MIDI hardware; makes no sound in openDAW.
MIDIOutput.limits: The sound is whatever hardware is connected.

WclapInstrument.sound: A third-party CLAP plugin instrument; its sound depends on the plugin.
WclapInstrument.limits: Name the plugin, never describe its sound.

Arpeggio.sound: Turns held chords into tempo-synced note patterns (up, down, up-down, random).
Arpeggio.limits: Needs held chords or notes to work with; turns sustained parts into busy ones.

Pitch.sound: Transposes notes by octaves, semitones and cents before the instrument.
Pitch.limits: Moves every note by the same interval; not key-aware harmony.

Velocity.sound: Pulls note velocities toward a target, offsets them and adds random variation.
Velocity.limits: Changes only how hard notes hit; how much that's heard depends on the instrument's velocity response.

Zeitgeist.sound: Swing and shuffle: pushes off-beat notes later for a groove.
Zeitgeist.limits: Moves timing only; doesn't add notes or change velocity.

Spielwerk.sound: A user-written script MIDI effect; what it does depends on the script.
Spielwerk.limits: Name the script, never describe what it does.

WclapMidiEffect.sound: A third-party CLAP note effect; what it does depends on the plugin.

Compressor.sound: Evens out dynamics; with fast settings adds punch, with sidechain ducks one part under another.
evokes: sidechain pump under a four-on-the-floor kick
Compressor.limits: Doesn't make a quiet part louder overall by itself (that's the fader); heavy settings flatten transients.

Maximizer.sound: Brickwall limiter with make-up gain: louder and denser, peaks held at the ceiling.
Maximizer.limits: Pushed hard it squashes transients and sounds flat or distorted. Usually last on the master.

Gate.sound: Cuts the signal below a threshold: removes noise and tails, or chops a sound rhythmically with a sidechain.
Gate.limits: Doesn't change tone; set badly it chatters or cuts notes short.

Revamp.sound: Seven-band parametric EQ (high-pass, shelves, three bells, low-pass): changes tonal balance cleanly.
Revamp.limits: Shapes existing tone only; can't add harmonics a sound doesn't have (use Waveshaper or Fold for that).

StereoTool.sound: Volume, pan, stereo width and phase utilities; no colour of its own.
StereoTool.limits: Can widen only what already has stereo difference; a mono source stays mono.

Tidal.sound: Tempo-synced tremolo and auto-pan: rhythmic volume or pan movement, smooth to choppy.
Tidal.limits: Moves volume and pan only, not tone.

Delay.sound: Tempo-synced stereo echo with ping-pong, filtered feedback and modulation: from slapback to long dub trails.
evokes: tape echo and dub sound-system delays
Delay.limits: High feedback builds up and can run away; long delays blur busy parts.

Reverb.sound: Light Freeverb-style algorithmic reverb: plain, slightly metallic room-to-hall space at low CPU.
Reverb.limits: Less lush and dense than Dattorro; long tails sound grainier.

DattorroReverb.sound: Dense, smooth plate-style reverb with modulated tails, up to infinite decay. Lush and shimmering.
DattorroReverb.limits: Muddies low parts (bass, kick) if put on them; long tails blur a busy mix.

Convolver.sound: Convolution with an impulse response: real rooms, halls, springs, plates or cabinets, as realistic as the IR. Can also be a creative texture.
Convolver.limits: Sounds like its impulse response; describe it by the IR. About four times Dattorro's CPU.

Crusher.sound: Bit-depth and sample-rate reduction: gritty, aliased, digital lo-fi, from subtle grain to 8-bit destruction.
Crusher.limits: Harsh and fizzy rather than warm; for warm saturation use Waveshaper (Tanh or Asymmetric).

Waveshaper.sound: Saturation and distortion by transfer curve: soft tube-like warmth (Tanh, Arctan, Asymmetric) to harsh buzz (Hardclip).
Waveshaper.limits: Adds harmonics and loudness; heavy settings lose low-end tightness.

Fold.sound: Wavefolding: folds peaks back for complex, metallic, bell-like harmonics, unlike clipping.
Fold.limits: Changes timbre drastically; not a subtle warmth effect.

Autotune.sound: Pitch correction to a key and scale, from transparent tuning to the hard robotic stepped effect.
Autotune.limits: Needs a single, monophonic voice or instrument; chords and drums confuse it.

Vocoder.sound: Imprints one sound's spectral shape (usually a voice) on another (usually a synth): talking synths and robot voices.
Vocoder.limits: Needs a carrier and a modulator; with no modulator signal it's silent or flat.

NeuralAmp.sound: Neural models of amps, pedals and cabinets; sounds like the model loaded.
NeuralAmp.limits: Name the model loaded; off limits to agents (models come from tone3000.com).

AudioEffectComposite.sound: Runs several effect chains in parallel and blends them back; sounds like its branches.

StereoComposite.sound: Processes left and right through separate chains; sounds like its branches.

FrequencySplit.sound: Splits into 2–4 frequency bands with a chain each; sounds like its bands' effects.

AudioSink.sound: Routing only: sends the signal at its point in the chain to a bus. No sound of its own.

Werkstatt.sound: A user-written script effect; what it does depends on the script.
Werkstatt.limits: Name the script, never describe what it does.

Wclap.sound: A third-party CLAP effect plugin; what it does depends on the plugin.
